# Copilot adoption support model

Template id: `adoption-support-model`

Responsible skill: `copilot-adoption:adoption-support-model`. The support summary also feeds the support row of the
`adoption-plan` template.

Use this document to agree where every kind of Copilot need goes, who answers it and how the programme learns from it.
Every fact the organisation must supply is marked `[To confirm: ...]`; replace the marker when the fact is confirmed,
and never fill it with a guess. Example rows are fictional and are there to be replaced or deleted. Support data is
reported by category, team or audience only, never for named individuals. Support for individual agents and AI
solutions is set out in each solution's own support model, not here.

## 1. Summary

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Audiences in scope | [To confirm: organisation, business unit or waves] |
| Copilot experiences in scope | [To confirm: for example Copilot Chat, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Cowork, agent awareness] |
| Support model owner | [To confirm: name and role] |
| IT service owner | [To confirm: name and role] |
| Security and privacy owner for the data exposure route | [To confirm: name and role] |
| Linked adoption plan | [To confirm: reference] |
| Linked Champions charter | [To confirm: reference, or "none yet"] |
| Status | Draft / Agreed / Superseded |
| Review date | [To confirm: date] |

## 2. Support principles

Agree these with the owners above. Edit to fit, but keep the intent.

- Each kind of need has one route, and users can find it from the getting-started page.
- Champions give first-line peer guidance within their agreed time and boundary; they are not the help desk.
- Suspected data exposure is reported immediately through the security route, at any hour it is staffed.
- Reports of wrong, harmful or misleading answers are recorded and reviewed, never closed as user error alone.
- Repeated questions are fixed at source, in guidance, onboarding or scenarios.

## 3. Support tiers

| Tier | Handles | Owner | Hours | How users reach it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Self-help | Getting started, approved use, starting scenarios, known issues | [To confirm] | Always available | [To confirm: page or site] |
| Peer guidance (Champions) | How-to questions in their own teams, prompt tips | [To confirm: Champions programme owner] | [To confirm: within agreed Champion time] | [To confirm: community channel, local Champion] |
| Office hours | Demonstrations, discussion, recurring themes | [To confirm] | [To confirm: rhythm] | [To confirm: calendar link location] |
| Service desk | Access, licence assignment, sign-in, app faults, errors | [To confirm] | [To confirm] | [To confirm: portal or phone route] |
| Admin and vendor escalation | Tenant settings, service issues, Microsoft support requests | [To confirm: administrator role] | [To confirm] | Via the service desk only |
| Security route | Suspected data exposure, oversharing, sensitive content in answers | [To confirm] | [To confirm: including out of hours] | [To confirm: route] |
| Intake | Ideas for shared prompts, Cowork tasks, agents or automation | [To confirm: intake owner or CoE] | [To confirm] | [To confirm: form or channel] |

## 4. Triage categories and routing

| Category | Fictional example | First route | Escalation | Target response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| How-to | "How do I summarise a long thread?" | Self-help, then Champions or office hours | Adoption lead for repeated themes | [To confirm] |
| Access | "Copilot isn't showing in my app" | Service desk | Administrators | [To confirm] |
| Fault | An error affecting many users | Service desk | Administrators, then Microsoft support | [To confirm] |
| Answer quality | "It gave me a wrong figure from a report" | Verification guidance; record the pattern | Adoption lead; agent owner where an agent is involved | [To confirm] |
| Data concern | "It showed me a document I shouldn't see" | Security route immediately | Permissions remediation owner | [To confirm] |
| Harmful or inappropriate output | "The answer was offensive" | Security route or responsible AI contact | [To confirm: responsible AI owner] | [To confirm] |
| Idea | "Could an agent prepare onboarding packs?" | Intake | CoE | [To confirm] |

Complete this checklist before an agent is shared with its audience, and again before its audience widens. Every fact

any reviewer means the release decision is "Not ready", whatever the date.

# Part B. Governance framework

## B1. Principles

[To confirm: for example business-owned, proportionate, human accountability explicit, govern once and repeat everywhere.]

## B2. Governance areas

Classify by the highest applicable factor: reach, data sensitivity, autonomy, impact on people and external exposure.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Individual productivity | [To confirm] | Acceptable-use starter, approved tools, human verification | None | Not applicable |

| 4 | External or high-impact | [To confirm] | Full assurance, human oversight, escalation, incident response, executive risk acceptance | All gates, formal evidence | [To confirm: executive role], in writing |

creates a status.

| Dimension | Not yet | Meets | Strong |
|---|---|---|---|
| Real work | Demo or invented task | A task from the person's own role or an assigned lab exercise | A recurring task valued by the team |

| Verification | Output used without checking | Output checked against its source; the check is described | The check is built into a reusable pattern |
| Judgement | No sense of limits | Notes where AI did not help or got it wrong | Explains when they would not use AI for this task |
| Transfer | Only the author could repeat it | Someone else could follow it | A colleague has used it |

# Champion capability framework and evidence rubric

Template id: `champion-capability-framework`

Responsible skills: `champions:capability-framework` (sections 1 to 5) and `champions:evidence-assessment`
(sections 6 and 7).

Use this framework to define what a Champion can demonstrably do, how they show it, how evidence is assessed and how
progress is recorded. Every fact the organisation must supply is marked `[To confirm: ...]`; replace the marker when
the fact is confirmed, and never fill it with a guess. Example content is fictional and is there to be replaced or
deleted. The framework assesses evidence of practice, never the person, and is never used to rank anyone.

## 1. Framework details

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Framework owner | [To confirm: name and role] |
| Approved tools for Champions | [To confirm: reference to the approved tools list] |
| Agent building allowed for Champions? | [To confirm: Yes, under which governance / No, the agent capability covers judging use cases and evaluating approved agents] |
| Self-service guidance or advisor agent that uses this framework | [To confirm: what it is and who owns it] |
| Version and date | [To confirm] |
| Next review | [To confirm: date] |

## 2. Capability cards

Training is one route, not the gate. Both options lead to the same verification criteria.

| Element | Chat capability | Productivity capability | Agent capability |
|---|---|---|---|
| Objective | Use Copilot Chat effectively and safely for real tasks - clear prompts, refinement, relevant context, verified output | Use Copilot across the Microsoft 365 apps to produce useful, validated outputs from recurring work, and help a colleague do the same | Explain what agents are, judge good and poor use cases and, where approved, configure a basic agent and test its behaviour |
| Training option | [To confirm: session plus guided exercise on own non-sensitive work] | [To confirm] | [To confirm] |
| Evidence option | Two or three real examples with prompt, refinement, output, check applied and what changed | Before-and-after account of a recurring task, a reusable prompt pattern and evidence a colleague used it | A note on one good and one poor agent candidate, plus a governed basic build with owner and tests, or evaluation notes on an approved agent |
| Verification criteria | Every rubric dimension at least Meets; refinement and choice of context visible | Every dimension at least Meets; output validated against its source; transfer shown | Every dimension at least Meets; sound use-case reasoning; tests with expected and observed behaviour; intake record for any build |
| Outcome | Chat verified; tracker updated; next milestone is productivity | Productivity verified; pattern offered to the scenario catalogue; next milestone is agents | Agent verified; eligible for the Champion Challenge |

Local adjustments to the capabilities: [To confirm]

## 3. Learning session map

Sessions stay open to the whole workforce. The guided exercise, not attendance, is what counts as evidence.

| Session | Rhythm | Open to | Counts towards | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Getting started and approved use | [To confirm] | Everyone | Joining the community | [To confirm] |
| Copilot Chat | [To confirm] | Everyone | Chat capability, training option | [To confirm] |
| Copilot in the Microsoft 365 apps, including meetings and collaboration in Teams | [To confirm] | Everyone | Productivity capability, training option | [To confirm] |
| Agent design and evaluation | [To confirm] | Everyone; building limited to approved makers | Agent capability, training option | [To confirm] |

## 4. Submission guide

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| How to submit | [To confirm: secure route with access limited to assessors and the programme owner] |
| What to redact | Personal data, client or confidential information, anything you would not share with the whole organisation |
| Retention period for evidence | [To confirm: agreed with the data protection lead] |
| Promised turnaround | [To confirm] |

## 5. Evidence rubric

Rate each dimension from the evidence alone. A capability is verified when every dimension is at least Meets and its
specific verification criteria are met. Strong is used for feedback, not ranking.

| Dimension | Not yet | Meets | Strong |
|---|---|---|---|
| Real work | Example is a demo or invented task | Example comes from the person's actual role | Example addresses a recurring, valued task for the team |
| Safe use | Sensitive data shared or unapproved tool used | No sensitive data shared; approved tools only | Explains choices about what not to share |
| Verification | No check of the output | Output checked; the check is explained | Check is built into a reusable pattern |
| Transferability | Only the submitter could repeat it | Someone else could reuse the pattern | A colleague has already reused it |
| Reflection | No account of limitations | Says what did not work and why | Shows how the approach was improved as a result |

> Fictional example: a submission shows a prompt used to summarise a supplier contract, a refined second prompt, the
> summary produced, and a note that the person compared every date and value against the contract before using it.
> Verification is rated Meets.

## 6. Assessment procedure

| Element | Entry |
|---|---|
| Assessment lead | [To confirm] |
| Assessor pool and training date | [To confirm] |
| Calibration rhythm | [To confirm: for example quarterly and when new assessors join] |
| Conflict rule | Assessors do not assess people they manage or know well; reassign |
| Both routes | Guided exercises and direct submissions are assessed against the same criteria |
| Second assessor | When unsure between ratings, for the agent capability and for disputed cases |
| Champion Challenge | Assessed on impact, reusability, quality and strategic alignment, using the `champion-challenge-catalogue` |
| Outcomes | Verified / Not yet (feedback and invitation to resubmit) / Returned unassessed (sensitive or incomplete evidence) |
| Feedback standard | Specific feedback on every dimension; for each Not yet, what would reach Meets; always the next milestone |

# Copilot Champions guide

Template id: `champion-guide`

Responsible skill: `champions:champion-recruitment`. The guide summarises the programme set out in the
`champion-programme-charter`, and is the source that self-service guidance or an advisor agent designed through
`champions:champion-advisor` explains to participants.

This is the guide prospective and current Champions read. Write it in plain language for participants, not for the
programme team. Every fact the organisation must supply is marked `[To confirm: ...]`; replace the marker when the
fact is confirmed, and never fill it with a guess. Example content is fictional and is there to be replaced or deleted.
Champions are selected on declared interest, skills and availability, and the programme never ranks individuals.

## Guide details

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Programme name | [To confirm] |

| Executive sponsor | [To confirm: name and role] |

## 1. Why the programme exists

[To confirm: the purpose statement from the charter, in one or two sentences]

> Fictional example: "We want every team to have someone who can show colleagues how to use Copilot safely and
> usefully in their own work, and who helps good ideas reach the right place."

## 2. What a Champion does, and what a Champion does not do

| Champions do | Champions do not |
|---|---|
| Use Copilot safely and responsibly in their own work, and show others how | Replace the service desk or formal training |
| Share prompts, examples and success stories | Approve solutions, agents or releases |
| Help colleagues in their own team with "how do I" questions | Act as solution architects |
| Promote approved tools and the organisation's AI guidance | Make governance or policy decisions |
| Spot ideas and send them to the right route | Build high-risk or externally facing solutions outside the Centre of Excellence |
| Take part in the community and give feedback | Become a queue for every AI request |

Where things go instead: faults and access to [To confirm: service desk route]; suspected data exposure to [To
confirm: security route]; ideas to [To confirm: intake route]; formal training to [To confirm: learning calendar].

## 3. Time commitment

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Time agreed for the role | [To confirm: for example hours per month] |
| How your manager confirms it | [To confirm: manager confirmation in section 11] |
| What happens if your workload changes | Talk to your manager and the programme owner; you can pause or step back at any time without it being treated as failure |

## 4. Who can join

Anyone in scope who wants the role and whose manager agrees the time. You do not need to be an expert: there is a
training route for people still learning. We aim for Champions in every team, site and type of role, including
frontline and part-time colleagues.

In scope: [To confirm: business units, locations, roles]

Selection uses only what you tell us (your interest, skills and availability) and the coverage the programme needs. It
never uses performance ratings, talent lists or Copilot usage data. If there are more volunteers than places, we
prioritise teams and sites without a Champion and offer everyone else the waiting list and open learning sessions.

## 5. The journey

| Stage | What you do | How it is confirmed |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Join the community | Agree time with your manager, join the community and the learning sessions | Manager confirmation |
| 2. Verify Chat capability | Show effective, responsible use of Copilot Chat | Training route or evidence route, assessed against published criteria |
| 3. Verify productivity capability | Create useful, checked outputs with Copilot across the Microsoft 365 apps | Training route or evidence route |
| 4. Verify agent capability | Explain agents, judge good use cases and, where approved, configure and test a basic agent | Training route or evidence route |
| 5. Complete a Champion Challenge | Deliver one practical contribution that helps others | Challenge assessment |
| 6. Recognised Champion | Keep modelling good practice and supporting colleagues | Renewal at [To confirm: period] |

Detailed criteria: [To confirm: link to the published capability framework and challenge catalogue]

## 6. Two routes to each capability

| Route | For whom | What it involves |
|---|---|---|
| Training route | People building their skills | [To confirm: sessions plus a guided exercise on your own work] |
| Evidence route | Experienced users | [To confirm: submit practical evidence directly against the criteria] |

Both routes are assessed against the same criteria. Assessors judge the evidence, not the person. If you disagree with
an outcome, you can ask for a review: [To confirm: appeal route].

Recognition is based on verified capability and contribution, never on attendance or how much you use Copilot.

## 10. What the CoE is and is not (Starter)

The CoE is:

- a business transformation capability, owned by the business unit that benefits;
- a structured delivery function with one backlog;
- a governance framework applied in proportion to risk;
- the home of opportunity management and knowledge management;
- the place where value and return are measured against baselines.

The CoE is not:

- an IT project: the business owns priorities, knowledge, adoption and benefits;
- a monthly reporting group: forums exist to take decisions;
- a technology experiment: work starts from a business outcome;
- a queue of requests for the central AI team: ideas arrive with an owner and a framed problem; the CoE provides method, assurance and patterns.

remove rows, then fill each cell with R (responsible), A (accountable), C (consulted) or I (informed). Every row has

release. Mark roles that do not yet exist `[To confirm: role to be appointed]`.

| Adoption | C | A | R | C |
| [To confirm: any further summary row] | | | | |

business owner the A for its benefit and each knowledge owner the A for their content.

| Deploy: test against the acceptance threshold | | C | A | C | R | | | | | |

# Opportunity canvas

Template id: `opportunity-canvas`
Responsible skills: `opportunity-management:problem-framing` (sections 1 to 3), `opportunity-management:ai-suitability`
(section 4) and `opportunity-management:risk-classification` (section 5)

One canvas per opportunity, carried from intake to decision. An opportunity does not enter delivery until sections 1 to
5 are complete. Anything not yet known stays marked `[To confirm: ...]`; never estimate a figure and record it as measured.

## 1. Request

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Opportunity reference | [To confirm: reference] |
| Date received | [To confirm: date] |
| Raised by (role) | [To confirm: role, for example a Champion or manager] |
| Original request, verbatim | [To confirm: request in the requester's words] |
| Candidate solution named by requester, if any | [To confirm: solution, recorded for suitability to test] |

## 2. Framed problem

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Problem statement (no technology named) | [To confirm: one or two sentences] |
| Business owner (role) and date agreed | [To confirm: role and date] |
| Affected roles and approximate numbers | [To confirm: roles and numbers] |
| Current cost (time, delay, quality, risk or experience) | [To confirm: description and measure] |
| Baseline | [To confirm: measured value, or how and by when it will be measured] |
| Expected outcome | [To confirm: change sought in the measure] |
| Strategic outcome supported | [To confirm: outcome reference, or "none"] |
| Possible duplicates elsewhere | [To confirm: references, or "none found"] |
| Early problem type (process issue, education gap, repetitive task, knowledge issue, business data workflow) | [To confirm: type, a signal for suitability rather than a decision] |
| Backlog entry reference and stage | [To confirm: reference; capture, assessment, delivery, live or value tracking] |

Fictional example, for illustration only: "Contract managers spend most of Monday compiling site reports from emails,
and a third of reports arrive late."

## 3. Early signals

| Signal | Yes, no or to confirm | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Personal, confidential or regulated data involved | [To confirm: answer] | [To confirm: note] |
| Outputs reach customers, partners or the public | [To confirm: answer] | [To confirm: note] |
| Informs decisions about people, money, safety or rights | [To confirm: answer] | [To confirm: note] |
| Relies on knowledge with no clear owner | [To confirm: answer] | [To confirm: note] |

Framing status: [To confirm: framed, awaiting owner, awaiting baseline, stopped (with reason) or merged]

## 4. AI suitability decision

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Rung chosen (0 no AI to 6 engineered solution), per part if combined | [To confirm: rung] |
| Rungs rejected and why | [To confirm: reasons] |
| Why AI beats process change, ordinary automation, training or an existing capability | [To confirm: reasoning, or "AI not recommended"] |
| Preconditions | [To confirm: preconditions] |
| Open questions | [To confirm: questions] |
| Decided by (role) and date | [To confirm: role and date] |

## 5. Risk tier record

Rate each factor 0 to 4 with one sentence of evidence. The tier is the highest rating, never an average. Anything shared
beyond its creator is at least tier 1. Tiers are a proposed CopilotForge convention to validate against local policy.

| Factor | Rating | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Impact if wrong | [To confirm: rating] | [To confirm: evidence] |
| Reach | [To confirm: rating] | [To confirm: evidence] |
| Data sensitivity | [To confirm: rating] | [To confirm: evidence] |
| Autonomy | [To confirm: rating] | [To confirm: evidence] |

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Risk tier | [To confirm: 0 to 4] |
| Minimum governance posture | [To confirm: posture for the tier] |
| Reviewer gates required | [To confirm: for example security-privacy, evaluation-quality, design-authority, responsible-ai] |
| Gate evidence the delivery team must produce | [To confirm: evidence by gate] |
| Redesign options considered (reach, data, autonomy) | [To confirm: options and decision] |
| Security and privacy record (tier 2 and above) | [To confirm: ai-risk-assessment reference] |
| Re-classification triggers | Wider audience, new data or connectors, new actions, external exposure, change of owner, incident |
| Governance areas checked (security, privacy, data ownership, compliance, human accountability) | [To confirm: answer or gap for each] |
| Human role accountable for outcomes | [To confirm: role] |
| Data and knowledge owners | [To confirm: roles] |
| Classified by (role) and date | [To confirm: role and date] |
| Tier lowered? Rationale and risk owner | [To confirm: rationale, or "not lowered"] |

## 6. Readiness to enter delivery

| Gate condition | Met |
|---|---|
| Named business owner | [To confirm: yes or no] |
| Clear problem statement | [To confirm: yes or no] |
| Expected outcome and baseline (or plan) | [To confirm: yes or no] |
| Initial risk classification | [To confirm: yes or no] |
